# Results

## Free generation selects packages, not wrappers

Amplifying frozen dual-effect features on 20 held-out prompts moves
article preference toward `an` on every prompt, but almost never
preserves content. Concrete twins include
`a pilot`\(\rightarrow\)`an aviator`,
`a lawyer`\(\rightarrow\)`an attorney`, and
`a physicist`\(\rightarrow\)`an astronomer`.
@tbl-packaging reports the clincher rates: trajectory-like package
switches dominate; wrapper-like repairs are exactly zero; illicit
`an`+consonant mismatches stay at zero. Matched controls do not
reproduce the package switch.

| Condition | \(N\) | Art.\(\rightarrow\)`an` | Content preserved | Class shift | Wrapper | Trajectory | Twin match |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S1 amplify \(5\times\) | 20 | 1.00 | 0.05 | 0.95 | 0.00 | 0.95 | 0.35 |
| S1 matched control | 20 | 0.70 | 1.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| S3 amplify \(5\times\) | 20 | 0.70 | 0.95 | 0.05 | 0.00 | 0.05 | 0.00 |

: Free-generation packaging versus wrapper metrics (held-out occupations).
S1 is dual-effect; S3 is content-ish. Controls are activation-matched.
{#tbl-packaging}

An earlier frozen LoF pair that repaired the source mismatch
`a ophthalmologist`\(\rightarrow\)`an ophthalmologist` likewise failed as
a content-preserving transfer: on held-out data it flipped many
expected-`a` controls to `an` and changed content words on 37/107
prompts, with **zero** grammar-only repairs that kept the noun fixed
(@fig-generalization; bridge details in Appendix~A).

![Held-out frozen-pair transfer changes articles and content together rather than repairing grammar alone.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure3_generalization.png){#fig-generalization width=82%}

## Selection rule and dose do not open a wrapper window

Changing how features are selected does not rescue modular H1 behavior
(@fig-selection). Across S1--S4 at \(5\times\) amplify, wrapper-like rate
is exactly 0.00. Only S1 is strongly trajectory-like (0.95); S2/S3 stay
near 0.05; S4 (competing `a`) produces neither wrappers nor
`an`-packages under amplification. S1 recovers the same dual-effect
family as the clincher (including `L12/F6229`, `L10/F2930`); S4 recovers
the historical ophthalmologist competing pair among its top features, but
amplifying it pushes toward `a` packages rather than content-preserving
grammar edits.

![No selection rule yields held-out wrapper-like repair; dual-effect S1 is almost purely trajectory-like.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure4_selection_ablation.png){#fig-selection width=78%}

A dose sweep on S1 likewise finds **no wrapper window**
(@fig-dose). As gain rises from \(1.5\times\) to \(8\times\), content
preservation falls from 0.90 to 0.05 while trajectory-like rate rises
from 0.10 to 0.95; wrapper-like rate remains 0.00 at every point. Mild
doses mostly do little; stronger doses buy package switches, not
grammar-only edits.

![Dose–response for dual-effect features: trajectory-like rate rises with gain; wrapper-like rate stays at zero.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure5_dose_response.png){#fig-dose width=78%}

## Dual lock and twin tetrad confirm packaging, not wrappers

If modular planning existed as an editable wrapper, amplifying
article-moving features while locking content-supporting features should
raise wrapper-like success above article-push alone. Under free
generation it does not (@fig-dual): content-lock alone (S3) preserves
nouns (\(\approx 0.95\)) but barely moves articles; article-push (S1)
and dual S1+S3 both remain \(\approx 95\%\) trajectory-like with
wrapper-like and illicit mismatch rates at 0.00. The system re-bundles
into legal packages (`an aviator`, `an attorney`) rather than producing
`an`+`pilot`.

![Content-lock preserves nouns but does not move articles; dual intervention still class-switches into legal packages.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure6_dual_lock.png){#fig-dual width=82%}

On pre-specified twins, a causal tetrad shows sufficiency and specificity
of package selection relative to matched controls (@fig-tetrad):
baseline and LoF (zero S1) remain `a pilot` / `a lawyer`; GoF (amplify
S1) selects `an aviator` / `an attorney`; control amplify does not.
Simple zeroing does not flip these baselines---necessity is
incomplete---but the positive causal role of the frozen set in selecting
the twin chunk is clear.

![Gain-of-function selects the vowel-initial twin package; matched random amplifications do not.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure7_causal_tetrad.png){#fig-tetrad width=82%}

## Pasting native \(b\) restores native \(c\)

The packaging suite still leaves open a modular objection: perhaps nouns
change only because the intervened article remains in context
(\(b\to c\)). Under selective article-step intervention with clamps
**off** at the noun step, free S1 amplify remains trajectory-like
(\(\approx 95\%\)), but forcing the native article yields content
preservation \(\approx 1.0\): e.g., free `an aviator` becomes `a pilot`
after pasting `a` (@fig-force-native). This isolates a real \(b\to c\)
edge. It does **not** yet refute independent \(C\to c\), because content
clamps were absent at \(c\).

![Free dual-effect intervention switches packages; pasting the native article restores the native noun.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure8_selective_force_native.png){#fig-force-native width=88%}

## Fixed \(b\), content on at \(c\): within-class null

@tbl-fixed-b and @fig-fixed-b report the corrected assay. Across eight
occupation families, S3 amplify (\(5\times\)/\(8\times\)), S3 zero,
hint-contrast amplify, and matched controls yield **zero** within-class
noun switches under fixed native \(b\) with clamps kept on at \(P\).
Same-class noun logits remain \(\approx 5\) below the source noun.
Protocol smoke tests confirm content-on versus content-off differ at the
logit level, so the assay is not collapsing by construction. S2
(article-ish) still moves article logits under paste-native while content
stays native---a licensing handle compatible with H2, not a modular
content dial.

| Condition | \(c\to c\) | Content \(\Delta\) | Match same-class | Mean \(\Delta\)(same$-$src) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | \(-4.90\) |
| S3 amp \(5\times\) / \(8\times\) / zero | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | \(\approx -4.9\) |
| Hint-contrast amp \(5\times\) | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | \(-4.91\) |
| Control amp \(5\times\) | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | \(-4.92\) |

: Fixed-\(b\), content-on-at-\(c\) within-class rates (8 families).
{#tbl-fixed-b}

![Corrected fixed-\(b\) assay: binary within-class outcomes are all zero; same-class nouns stay ~5 logits below source.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure9_fixed_b_content_on.png){#fig-fixed-b width=80%}

## Escape hatches: per-noun sparse features and residual directions

A modular defender might blame the wrong sparse objects. We therefore
(i)~select Latent-Planning-style per-example features for each
same-class target (positive target attribution, low article attribution;
plus target$-$source contrast) and (ii)~steer a dense MLP-in residual
direction toward the same-class noun. Both use the same fixed-\(b\),
content-on schedule on three twin families (@tbl-escape;
@fig-pernoun; @fig-residual).

| Handle | Best \(c\to c\) | Best \(\Delta\Delta\)(same$-$src) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Per-noun LP-target / contrast (amp \(5\times\)--\(8\times\)) | 0.00 | \(+0.29\) |
| Residual content steer \(\alpha=1\)--\(8\) | 0.00 | \(\approx 0.08\) |
| Residual random control \(\alpha=1\)--\(8\) | 0.00 | \(\approx 0.15\) |

: Escape-hatch assays under fixed \(b\). Neither per-noun sparse selection
nor residual MLP-in steering opens a within-class dial; residual content
steering does not beat random controls.
{#tbl-escape}

Every force-on continuation remained on the baseline noun
(`pilot`/`lawyer`/`psychologist`). Per-noun sparse selection does not
open a dial (@fig-pernoun); residual content steering does not beat
matched-norm random controls (@fig-residual).

![Per-noun LP-style and contrast features under fixed \(b\): within-class outcomes remain zero; same-class nouns stay ~5 logits below source.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure10_per_noun_fixed_b.png){#fig-pernoun width=80%}

![Dense residual (MLP-in) content steering under fixed \(b\): within-class outcomes remain zero for content and random directions.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure11_residual_fixed_b.png){#fig-residual width=82%}
